analysis.title: GS Blekos - GOAL Kickstart / US Consumer Outlook / US Semis / DC in Europe / RHM / Pluxee / Indus Heatmap / Naturgy 10 Nov 2026
key_insights: GS stays overweight equities over 3m and 12m, citing earnings support, lighter positioning and lower valuations into year-end. It stays overweight cash because near-term volatility may linger on AI uncertainty and Middle East tensions.

GS sees three paths to a rebound in risk appetite: easing AI concerns with signs of monetisation, rates relief helped by falling energy prices, and a larger decline of its RAI below -1, which improves the asymmetry for adding risk into year-end.
GS stays overweight bonds, favouring longer-duration bonds for their higher yields. It argues peaking nominal growth gives equities a better buffer.

GS US Economics expects 2027 consumer spending to grow 2.2% (Q4/Q4), near potential. It expects a softer start to the year from higher rates weighing on durables, elevated energy prices and lower nonprofit spending after the midterms. A pickup follows as inflation pressures abate and tax refunds and the reversal of benefit cuts make the fiscal impulse modestly positive.

GS flags downside risk to consumer spending from a fading wealth effect. It estimates the effect added over 0.4pp to spending growth in 2026 and should add about half as much in 2027, and it could weigh on spending if AI-related stocks keep declining.

GS Americas semiconductors note says the sector has pulled back and is at the center of tensions around the AI datacenter build. GS favours NVDA and AVGO in AI compute, which it says imply no growth from 2027.
In semi cap equipment, GS treats 2027 WFE as a baseline and prefers AMAT and LRCX.

GS says European datacenter growth is unaffected by the US midterms. It favours power generators with power land, connection points and the ability to sign energy supply contracts: Solaria (Buy, on CL), Drax (Buy), RWE (Buy, on CL), PPC (Buy) and Fortum (Neutral).
GS expects ongoing acceleration in European power grid capex, naming EON (Buy), and flags Buy-rated equipment makers Siemens Energy (on CL), Vestas and Nordex.
GS hosted a fireside chat with Rheinmetall CEO Armin Papperger covering German programmes, ammunition, naval, air defence, unmanned systems and cash conversion.

GS upgrades Pluxee to Neutral from Sell after share price underperformance and another reset of earnings expectations. The stock is down 31% since being added to the Sell List on October 14, 2024, underperforming the STOXX 600 and FTSE World Europe by 55pp.

GS attributes Pluxee's underperformance to regulatory headwinds, particularly in Brazil, and weaker-than-expected underlying operating revenue trends that drove material downward revisions to consensus earnings.
The note also includes a Europe multi-industry 3Q26 heatmap and a Naturgy piece on a renewable route to growth, with no detail in the extracted text.
